C20.03 adds the approved focused scalar CodingRate owner, retaining existing imports and the lightweight root boundary. C21.01 adds the focused SourceCodingAsymptotic owner for finite-iid almost-lossless families above entropy, preserving retained imports and the lightweight root boundary. C22.01 adds the attained finite-channel information-capacity core, retaining the root and semantic umbrella boundaries. C22.03 adds the focused product-capacity owner while preserving the root and semantic umbrella boundaries. C22.04 adds the focused standard-channel capacity owner for noiseless and input-independent channels. C22.05 adds the probability-only standard-channel owner and BSC capacity through the existing focused information owner. C23.01 adds the focused deterministic channel-code model, actual uniform-message laws and average error, retaining the lightweight root and semantic umbrella boundaries. No capacity/converse endpoint is introduced in this step. C23.02 adds the focused finite ChannelCoding owner for actual-law Markov/DPI and Fano-capacity bounds. It preserves every earlier direct import, the lightweight root and semantic umbrella boundaries; asymptotic imports remain a later step. C23.03 adds the focused ChannelCodingAsymptotic owner for vanishing-error rate tolerance and real limsup bounds. Eventual boundedness is proved from the finite converse, keeping focused limit imports out of finite code consumers and retaining the lightweight root and semantic aggregate boundaries. C23.04 extends the existing ChannelCodingAsymptotic owner with quantitative eventual above-capacity error, a positive eventual floor and nonvanishing-error consequences for eventual or infinitely-often fixed positive rate gaps. Existing imports and all lightweight root/semantic boundaries are retained.
import_approvals.consumer: Full-stack users import LeanInfoTheory.Shannon; the independently importing total-variation, coupling and continuity consumers verify focused access. Examples.ChannelOptimization independently imports the focused Topology owner for actual MI attainment and boundary/degeneracy consumers. Examples.FiniteProduct independently exercises its probability-only import. Examples.Iid independently imports Probability.Iid and exercises both non-iid block transports and sparse iid laws. Examples.ProductChannel exercises the new probability-only owner independently. Examples.TypicalSet independently exercises the finite owner without AEP. Examples.SourceCoding independently imports only SourceCoding and exercises the pair interface, exact error, success counting and the public selected-set existence and converse endpoints, including constructed fair, pure, singleton and empty-word cases. Examples.CodingRate privately exercises scalar boundaries and actual code padding into binary strings with exact error preservation and finite rate overhead. Examples.SourceCodingAsymptotic independently imports the focused owner and uses the same public family for vanishing error and eventual rate bounds, including pure and sparse sources. Examples.ProductChannelCapacity independently imports the focused owner for arbitrary correlated inputs, independent maximizing witnesses and empty/singleton products. Examples.StandardChannelCapacity independently imports that owner for actual uniform/pure attaining laws, non-pure constant output, sparse inputs and singleton alphabets. Examples.StandardChannels checks raw BSC masses and endpoints with only the probability owner; Examples.StandardChannelCapacity uses the objective, capacity and direct uniform-attainment formulas. Examples.ChannelCode independently imports only the focused channel-code owner for the law/error interface, unequal encoder fibers and singleton/zero/one-length boundaries. Examples.ChannelCoding exercises the actual-law Markov and information-processing chain, the finite Fano-capacity endpoint and normalized/error forms on a colliding correlated two-letter code and singleton/zero/one-length cases. Examples.ChannelCodingAsymptotic uses actual singleton-message families and a lossless noiseless family whose rates need not converge, applying both public asymptotic endpoints without a bounded/convergent-rate assumption. Examples.ChannelCodingAsymptotic adds positive-capacity noiseless finite/eventual quantitative consumers and a zero-capacity intermittent family with unbounded rate spikes and infinitely many zero-error lengths, distinguishing nonvanishing error from an eventual positive floor.

import_approvals.rationale: C23.03 exports eventually_codeRate_le_channelCapacity_add and limsup_codeRate_le_channelCapacity for one arbitrary dependent deterministic channel-code family with positive natural budgets and vanishing average error. A private helper derives eventual rate boundedness from the finite Fano-capacity inequality; nonnegative codeRate supplies the real limsup lower/coboundedness condition. No bounded-rate, convergent-rate, eventual-rate-cap or global positive-length premise is added. The two focused mathlib imports supply reciprocal-length limits and conditionally complete real limsup tools; ChannelCoding supplies the entire finite interface. Derived-bound and limit side-condition machinery remain private. No sequence structure, EReal-limsup wrapper, source-coding dependency, root export or simp attribute is introduced; at the C23.03 checkpoint, above-capacity error obstructions remained a later step. C23.04 now adds exactly eventually_one_sub_channelCapacity_div_sub_le_errorProbability, eventually_pos_le_errorProbability_of_eventually_le_codeRate, not_tendsto_errorProbability_zero_of_eventually_le_codeRate and not_tendsto_errorProbability_zero_of_frequently_channelCapacity_add_le_codeRate in the same BlockChannelCode namespace. The eventual rate lower bound R above capacity yields the quantitative eventual error bound and a positive error floor, deriving R>0 from capacity nonnegativity. A fixed positive gap occurring infinitely often rules out vanishing error for possibly unbounded rates without asserting an eventual floor or using an unguarded real limsup. These extensions reuse the existing three direct imports and finite pointwise error theorem; no new production module/import, public helper, alias, simp attribute, root export, EReal-limsup equivalence or strong-converse endpoint is added. C23.05 reconciles these unchanged six public family endpoints through private same-family composition rather than adding a sequence abstraction or production helper.
